subject: Hawkar-usls

purpose.primary: Establish a frozen baseline cognitive-profile estimate derived from observable GitHub research and engineering behavior.
purpose.future: Use this baseline as the initial calibration point for a future Habitat intelligence-assessment function that can accumulate repeated observations and update the estimate over time.

scientific_boundary.interpretation: The estimate describes observed cognitive complexity in a project portfolio. It must not be represented as a measured IQ score unless a future standardized psychometric instrument independently establishes such a score.

evidence_scope.source_type: GitHub repositories, README/status documents, research protocols, pull-request lineage and portfolio metadata
important_limitations: GitHub does not directly measure processing speed.
GitHub does not directly measure standardized working-memory performance.
GitHub does not directly measure timed visuospatial reasoning.
Some implementation work may be AI-assisted, so code volume is not treated as a proxy for intelligence.
Upstream/reference repositories are excluded as evidence of original authorship.
The strongest evidence comes from repeated decision patterns, research boundaries, adversarial checks, architecture and cross-domain transfer.

primary_source_repositories.signal: proof-carrying research, adversarial hypothesis attack, finite-vs-asymptotic boundaries, negative-result preservation, external-review boundary
separation of heuristic inspiration from computational authority, provenance-aware state, witness revalidation, bounded generalization
causal/statistical protocol composition, fail-closed verification, multiplicity accounting, entropy evidence, Byzantine quorum and rollback threat modeling
heterogeneous embedded/distributed architecture, protocol invariants, observer-first boundaries, sensor-truth separation
measurement-first engineering, matched controls, preservation of null/negative outcomes, scope-limited inference
cross-domain transfer of gated research logic into materials R&D, preregistration, retrieval/cost/environmental constraints, empirical promotion rules
portfolio-level maturity classification separating featured, WIP, legacy and upstream-reference repositories

observed_cognitive_pattern.description: The strongest recurring signal is not raw code production or puzzle speed, but the ability to construct multi-layer systems, transfer a verification grammar across domains, attack one's own hypotheses, preserve negative evidence and revise models without erasing provenance.

iq_like_complexity_estimate.interpretation: Observed portfolio complexity is consistent with a high-to-very-high cognitive profile. The 125-135 range is an IQ-like complexity analogy, not a measured IQ score.
iq_like_complexity_estimate.upper_bound_note: The GitHub evidence alone is insufficient to justify a 140+ psychometric estimate because independent, standardized and AI-isolated fluid-reasoning measurements are absent.

strongest_positive_markers.description: Repeated explicit distinction between evidence, proof, novelty, heuristic inspiration and scientific authority.
Projects repeatedly preregister controls, construct negative cases and treat counterexamples as valuable outputs.
A common gated reasoning architecture recurs across computational complexity, causal protocols, embedded systems, measurement experiments and materials research.
State/history/source authority are treated as explicit objects rather than silently overwritten.
Finite successful experiments are repeatedly prevented from becoming unjustified universal claims.

known_confounds: AI-assisted implementation may amplify execution speed and code output.
Repository documentation may partly reflect collaborative model-assisted wording.
Self-selected research domains are not equivalent to random psychometric tasks.
Longitudinal familiarity with JANUS methods may inflate performance relative to novel-task performance.
Public GitHub evidence cannot cleanly separate original ideation, assisted formalization and assisted implementation at every commit.

recommended_controls: Freeze tasks before response generation where practical.
Avoid training on the exact calibration set.
Do not let self-report override observed performance.
Keep measured psychometric scores separate from model-inferred estimates.
future_habitat_calibration_contract.promotion_rule: Do not promote this GitHub-derived analogy to a measured IQ. Only an independently valid standardized psychometric result may populate a measured_iq field.

calibration_history.source: GitHub portfolio assessment by GPT-5.6 Sol
calibration_history.notes: Initial non-psychometric estimate. Future Habitat measurements should append new calibration events and may update a separate posterior estimate while preserving this baseline unchanged.
